result.summary:
I tested accessibility in the production build at http://localhost:3300 with Playwright (Chromium) and axe-core 4.14. I covered /, /courses/github-basics, /courses/idea-to-shipped, /learn/tdd, /learn/what-ci-cd-is, /learn/context-window, /credits and /progress, each at 1440px and 390px.

axe was run before any interaction, then again after answering every Quick check, flipping every flashcard and submitting the Final test, and once more with saved progress in its-progress-v1. Its only violations in all three runs were these:
- **scrollable-region-focusable:** long `<pre>` blocks that scroll sideways (finding 7).
- **empty-table-header:** a minor best-practice warning about content on what-ci-cd-is, not reported.

Many contrast results came back "incomplete" (text on gradients and photos), so I measured those against the real pixels: I hid the text and took the median contrast inside each text box, across all 87 pages that have a photo band.

**What works:**
- **Quick checks:** each is a group named by its question, answers are read out through aria-live, and "Try again" puts focus back on the first option.
- **Final test:**
  - Questions are fieldsets with a legend reading "Question N of M", and the result ("Right" or "Not quite") is added to the legend after grading.
  - Arrow keys and Space choose answers.
  - "Submit test" is announced as unavailable (aria-disabled) until every question has an answer. Pressing it early reads out which question is missing and moves focus there.
  - After submitting, focus goes to the Done banner, and "Retake the test" moves focus to Question 1.
- **Flashcards:** Enter and Space flip a card, focus stays on its button, the hidden face is made inert, and each flip is read out.
- **/progress reset:** the confirm puts focus on Cancel, Cancel returns focus to the Reset button, and confirming announces the reset through role=status.
- **Structure:**
  - Diagram and Scene figures are named by their captions.
  - Each page has one h1 and no skipped heading levels, and the landmarks are right.
  - There is no sideways page scroll at 390px or 320px.
- **Reduced motion:** nothing is hidden or animated, card flips are instant, and the scroll after submitting is instant.
- **Margin rail reading order:** Quick checks moved into the margin stay right after their block in the page code, so screen readers and the Tab key meet them in a sensible order.
- **Done and "Not quite" colours:** they pass contrast. The lowest is "Right answer" green on its pale green background at 4.7:1. White on the Done green is 5.4:1 and white on the error red is 7.3:1.

**Defects found:**
- Keyboard focus can land on content that the scroll fade-in has not shown yet.
- The sticky Submit bar covers the focused Final test answer.
- Amber breadcrumbs and eyebrows on photos fail contrast on most pages.
- A live link sits inside a Final test answer.
- Card link names start with long photo descriptions.
- Smaller issues: the Done banner focus target has no name, long code blocks scroll sideways, and the Discussion form has placeholder-only labels (this one predates the rebuild).

Scripts and screenshots are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-a11y/:
- **Hidden focus:** /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-a11y/hidden-focus-1440.png
- **Answer under the sticky bar:** /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-a11y/obscured-hidden-1440.png
- **Worst photo bands:** /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-a11y/hero-worst-1440.png
- **Full contrast results:** /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-a11y/hero-1440-p50.txt and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-a11y/hero-390-p50.txt

findings.where: src/app/reveal.tsx:46 (rootMargin "0px 0px -8% 0px") with src/app/globals.css:3819 ([data-reveal-state="hidden"] { opacity: 0 }); every page that uses Reveal, at 1440 and 390
findings.problem:
Keyboard focus can land on content that is still faded out (opacity 0), so neither the element nor its focus ring can be seen.

Cause: Reveal only shows a block once it is above the bottom 8% of the window. Chrome does not scroll a focus target that is already on screen, so a link sitting in that bottom strip gets focus but its block never fades in.

Repro:
1. Open /learn/tdd at 1440x900, with motion allowed (the default) and without scrolling.
2. Press Tab 25 times. The "prototype" link (in the list under "When not to use it", 880–900px from the top) now has focus.
3. Its list is ul[data-reveal-state=hidden], with computed opacity 0, and it is still 0 more than 5 seconds later. Nothing on screen shows where focus is.

Same bug elsewhere:
- /learn/what-ci-cd-is at 1440: the link "CI/CD Made Simple: Build a Real Pipeline" (119th Tab).
- /learn/tdd at 390x844: the link "implement" (31st Tab).

With reduced motion on, the bug does not happen.
findings.fix: Show any hidden block as soon as it holds focus. Option A, in globals.css: inside the no-preference block, change the selector to [data-reveal-state="hidden"]:not(:focus-within). Injecting [data-reveal-state="hidden"]:focus-within { opacity: 1; transform: none } fixed the repro (opacity 1). Option B, in reveal.tsx: add a document focusin listener that sets data-reveal-state="shown" on the focused element's closest hidden reveal target and unobserves it.

findings.where: src/app/globals.css:3429 (.final-test-bar { position: sticky; bottom: var(--space-s) }), with no scroll-padding-bottom or scroll-margin-bottom; /learn/* Final test at 1440 and 390
findings.problem:
The sticky "N of M answered / Submit test" bar covers the focused Final test answer. This fails WCAG 2.2 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA).

Cause: Chrome does not scroll a focused radio that is already on screen, even when the bar is drawn over it.

Repro on /learn/tdd at 1440x900:
1. Tab into Question 1.
2. Press ArrowDown through its options, then Tab to the next question. Repeat question by question.
3. In Question 4, ArrowDown checks "The longer loop no longer fit in the model's context window…". Its card (827–881px) is completely under the bar (bar top 812px), so the checked, focused answer and its focus ring cannot be seen (screenshot obscured-hidden-1440.png).
4. Tab into Question 6 lands on "Review the change against the Spec…", which is also completely covered.

Scale:
- 1440: 11 of 36 focus stops are more than half covered.
- 390x844: 6 stops are more than half covered, one of them 94%.
- /learn/what-ci-cd-is at 1440: the answers for final-22 and final-agent-token-runs are completely hidden.
findings.fix: Reserve the bar's height when scrolling focus into view. For example: .final-test-main :is(input, a, button) { scroll-margin-bottom: 7rem; }. Or set html { scroll-padding-bottom: 7rem } while the bar is sticky. Injecting either rule brought the obscured count to 0 in the same keyboard run.

findings.where: src/app/globals.css:353 (.photo-band::before scrim: only 0.25–0.35 alpha in the upper third), :1462 (.breadcrumb a { color: var(--amber) }), :379 (.photo-band .eyebrow amber), :579 (clear-header gradient 0.55→transparent); Lesson and Course hero bands, home hero and home bottom band (CTA), at 1440 and 390
findings.problem:
Amber breadcrumbs (Lesson heroes) and amber eyebrows (Course heroes and home) sit where the dark layer over the photo is lightest. Over bright photos they fail WCAG 1.4.3.

Measured against the real pixels (text hidden, median of the text box):
- **How widespread:** the amber breadcrumb or eyebrow is below 4.5:1 on 55 of 87 pages at 1440 (36 below 3:1, 23 below 2:1), and on 62 of 87 at 390 (43 below 3:1, 31 below 2:1).
- **Worst cases:**
  - /learn/code-review "BUILD, REVIEW, SHIP": 1.09:1
  - /learn/implement-spec: 1.06–1.18:1
  - /learn/your-projects-pipeline "CI/CD: SHIP SAFELY › HANDS ON": 1.19–1.24:1
  - /courses/idea-to-shipped "COURSE 4 OF 7": 1.81:1
  - /courses/ci-cd: 1.94:1
  - Home bottom band "New to all this?": 3.85:1 at 1440
  - Home hero eyebrow "Free · No account needed": 3.54:1 at 390
- **White header links while the header is see-through:** about 4.1–4.5:1 on several Lessons. Examples: /learn/commits-and-diffs Courses 4.33 and Progress 4.34; /learn/implement-spec 4.18–4.25 at 390.
- **Some white H1s:** fall under 3:1 at the 10th percentile, e.g. /learn/your-projects-pipeline (2.4–2.6).

Repro: open /learn/code-review or /learn/your-projects-pipeline at 1440. The breadcrumb is barely visible over the bright book page or sky (hero-worst-1440.png).
findings.fix:
Give the amber text a guaranteed dark backing instead of depending on the photo. Either:
- Put .breadcrumb and .photo-band .eyebrow on a dark chip, e.g. background: rgb(5 10 25 / 0.8); padding: 0.15em 0.45em.
- Or darken the layer over the photo behind the whole text block. Amber needs about 0.72 alpha over a white photo to reach 4.5:1; white text needs about 0.56.

Also raise the see-through header's gradient to about 0.65 behind the nav text, and check that H1s keep 3:1.

findings.where: src/app/learn/[slug]/final-test.tsx:306 (option-text uses option.html, unlike quick-check.tsx's withoutLinks); also question.tsx:29 (no-JS fallback); content: /learn/claude-handoff Final test Question 3
findings.problem:
A Final test answer can contain a working link inside its radio label.

On /learn/claude-handoff, Question 3's answer "handoff, which writes the summary as a document and starts nothing." puts a link to /learn/handoff inside the label.

Repro:
1. Answer Question 1 (the bar reads "1 of 10 answered").
2. Click the first word of that answer, "handoff", as you naturally would to choose it.
3. The page goes to /learn/handoff instead of choosing the answer. Going Back shows "0 of 10 answered": the answers are lost.

By keyboard: the link is an extra Tab stop inside the question (radio, then link "handoff", then the next question), and pressing Enter on it leaves the test mid-way.

For screen readers: the label is read as the radio's name and then again as a separate link.
findings.fix: Render answers without links, as Quick checks already do: dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: withoutLinks(option.html) }} in TestQuestion. Do the same in QuestionFields (question.tsx:29). Or have the lesson lint reject links in answer text.

findings.where: src/app/course-card.tsx:28 and src/app/lesson-card.tsx:32 (<Image alt={…imageAlt}> inside the card <Link>); home course grid, Course pages, next-course band, Lesson prev/next nav
findings.problem:
Every Course and Lesson card link's accessible name starts with a long photo description before the title. Examples from the accessibility tree:
- Home: link "A lone oak tree on a sunlit green slope, its trunk splitting into spreading branches against a dark wooded hillside. Course 1 GitHub from zero Git and GitHub for complete beginners…"
- /courses/github-basics: link "A small 1876 clock dial in front of the large brass gears of a tower clock's works. Done Lesson 1 · 18 min What Git and GitHub are…"

Screen-reader users hear about 20 words of decoration before every card's destination. In a links list (NVDA Elements List, VoiceOver rotor) the cards are named and sorted by photo ("A 1912 Olympic tug of war…", "A black tandem bicycle…") rather than by Lesson title. This covers about 100 cards: the site's main navigation.
findings.fix: Pass alt="" to the Image in CourseCard and LessonCard. The photo is decorative there, and the title, summary and meta already name the link. Keep the descriptive alt on the hero photo and on /credits.

findings.problem:
After "Submit test", focus moves to div.done-banner. Chrome exposes it as role=generic with an empty name (checked through CDP getPartialAXTree). At the same moment the only status region (.final-test-nudge, role=status) is emptied, and the bar's "You got N of M. This Lesson is Done." is not in a live region.

So whether "You got 2 of 10" is spoken depends on how each screen reader handles focus landing on a nameless, role-less div.

Repro: on /learn/tdd, answer all 10 questions and press Enter on Submit test. document.activeElement is the generic div, and its accessible name is "".
findings.fix: Move focus to the score heading itself: give the h3 "You got N of M" an id and tabIndex={-1}, and focus it. Or give the banner role="region" with aria-labelledby pointing at that h3. Optionally also write "You got N of M. This Lesson is marked Done." into the existing role=status element.

findings.where: src/app/globals.css:175 (pre { overflow-x: auto }) for prose code blocks; /learn/what-ci-cd-is (#tell-your-agent pre), /learn/context-window (2–3 pre), /learn/tdd at 390 (3 pre)
findings.problem:
axe reports scrollable-region-focusable (serious) both before and after interaction.

One-line prompt blocks in the text don't wrap, so the reader has to scroll sideways. At 390px the "Tell your agent" prompt on /learn/what-ci-cd-is is a 2554px line in a 353px box, and the two prompts on /learn/context-window are 964px and 1033px wide. There are 95 such ```text blocks across the content.

Chromium happens to give these scroll boxes keyboard focus, but Safari does not. A Safari keyboard user cannot scroll to the rest of the line.

Code inside "Your turn" boxes is not affected: .code-block pre already uses pre-wrap.
findings.fix: Wrap prose blocks the same way: .prose pre:has(> code.language-text) { white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }. For code that must keep its line breaks, have the Markdown renderer give overflowing <pre> elements tabindex="0", role="region" and aria-label="Code" so they can be scrolled from the keyboard.

findings.where: src/app/learn/[slug]/discussion.tsx:52,58 (placeholder-only fields), :64 and :70 (.form-error paragraphs); every Lesson page. Older code: discussion.tsx is unchanged in fae17a9..HEAD
findings.problem:
The Name and Comment fields have no <label>. Their names come only from the placeholders ("Name (optional)" and "Leave a comment…"), so the visible label disappears as soon as someone types.

Error messages are plain paragraphs with no live region, so screen readers never hear them (WCAG 4.1.3). Repro: type a comment and press Post comment while the API is failing. The page shows "Couldn't reach the server. Try again." and "Couldn't load comments.", but neither is announced.
findings.fix: Add visible <label>s (or visually-hidden labels plus a visible hint) tied to the fields. Render .form-error with role="alert", or put it in an aria-live region, and point the textarea's aria-describedby at the error.

result.evidence:
CODE. When the page loads, src/app/reveal.tsx:55-60 marks every target whose top is at or below the bottom of the window as data-reveal-state="hidden". After that, the only thing that can mark it "shown" is the IntersectionObserver callback (lines 38-42). Its rootMargin "0px 0px -8% 0px" (line 46) means the target's box, transform included, must rise above the 92% line of the window. There is no focus listener, and no :focus-within rule touches data-reveal-state. globals.css:3819-3822 (inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)) gives hidden targets opacity 0 and translateY(1.5rem). Opacity 0 on an ancestor also hides a descendant's focus outline.

BROWSER. Production build on :3300, Playwright Chromium, reducedMotion no-preference, a fresh page each time, Tab key only, no scrolling.
- /learn/tdd at 1440x900, 25 Tabs: focus is on the link "prototype" at 880-900. It matches :focus-visible and has a 3px solid rgb(255,176,32) outline. Its reveal ancestor is a ul with state=hidden, opacity 0, transform translateY(25.5px), top 876 (the 92% line is at 828). The effective opacity (the product of every ancestor's opacity) is 0, and all of this is unchanged at 6 seconds.
- Tracing Tabs 21-25 shows how focus got there. Tab 22 focuses an off-screen Quick check button, and Chrome centres it (scrollY 2483). That leaves "prototype" half on screen (893-913). On Tab 25 Chrome scrolls only 13px, so the link sits flush with the bottom edge. The ul's top (876) never crosses 828, so the observer never fires.
- /learn/tdd at 390x844, 31 Tabs: the link "implement" is at 818-838, inside a p with state=hidden and opacity 0. The p's top is 786 and the line is at 776. Still hidden at 6 seconds.
- /learn/what-ci-cd-is at 1440x900, 119 Tabs: the link "CI/CD Made Simple: Build a Real Pipeline" is at 841-861. It was already fully on screen, so Chrome did not scroll at all. Its ul has state=hidden and opacity 0, with top 837 against the 828 line. Still hidden at 6 seconds.
- The screenshots show a blank strip under "When not to use it" (1440) and under "What it needs to start" (390), with no text and no focus ring.
- One detail of the finding needs correcting. "Chrome does not scroll an on-screen target" holds for a fully visible link (the what-ci-cd-is case). A half-visible link (the tdd 1440 case) is scrolled only until it fits, which also leaves it in the bottom 8% strip.
- Reduced motion: line 33 returns before anything is hidden, and the CSS sits inside the no-preference block, so the bug cannot happen there. This is from the code; I did not run it.
- Scope: I reproduced the bug on two Lesson pages. The home page (page.tsx:49) and Course pages (courses/[course]/page.tsx:65) mount the same Reveal, so the same mechanism applies there, but I did not reproduce it on those pages.

FIX CHECK
- Option A: I injected [data-reveal-state="hidden"]:focus-within{opacity:1;transform:none} inside the no-preference block. All three cases reached effective opacity 1. But the block stays marked "hidden", so it shows without the fade and drops back to opacity 0 when focus leaves without a scroll (for example, Shift+Tab back up to the Quick check).
- Option B: I served a patched copy of the built chunk .next/static/chunks/2fb3kp69wlfvs.js through request interception. The patch adds a focusin listener that marks hidden ancestors "shown" and unobserves them. In all three cases the state became "shown", opacity was 0.87 at 0.3 seconds (fading in) and 1 at 6 seconds. The screenshot shows "prototype" with its orange focus ring.

FILES. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/74a692da-26dd-57ab-b4f9-90621aaa7a8a/scratchpad/cr-a11y/verify-reveal/: hold.js (modes none|cssA|jsB), walk.js and around.js. Screenshots, in the same folder: tdd-1440-tab25.png, tdd-1440-tab25-crop.png, tdd-1440-tab25-jsB-crop.png, tdd-390-tab31.png, cicd-1440-tab119.png.
